label: Freight railroad
description: A freight railroad (Class I, regional or short line): subdivisions and yards, a dispatching center running CTC and PTC, train crews, mechanical and signal forces, the hazardous materials it hauls and the towns along the line.

vocabulary.facility: the railroad (subdivisions, yards, intermodal ramps and the dispatching center)
vocabulary.public: residents along the line, shippers and the communities the trains pass through
vocabulary.frontline: train crews, train dispatchers, yardmasters, track inspectors, signal maintainers, carmen, railroad police special agents
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the network operations and dispatching center

it: transportation management and car accounting system (waybills, car location)
customer portal and EDI with shippers and interchange partners
industry data exchanges (Umler equipment registry, car hire, AskRail responder app)
ot: computer-aided dispatching and CTC with code lines to field signal locations
wayside signals, track circuits and interlockings
PTC (I-ETMS onboard, wayside interface units, back office server, 220 MHz radio)
wayside defect detectors (hot bearing, dragging equipment, wheel impact)
hump yard process control (retarders and switches)

roles.name: Chief Operating Officer (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the service plan, train holds and reroutes, crew allocation, and the railroad's seat in unified command.

roles.name: Chief Train Dispatcher / Dispatching Center Manager
roles.description: Owns movement authority (CTC signals, track warrants), holds, and track-and-time protection for responders.

roles.name: Hazardous Materials Manager
roles.description: Owns the train consist given to responders, the hazmat contractor call-out, and the transfer or vent-and-burn recommendation.

roles.name: Cybersecurity Coordinator / CISO (Technical Lead)
roles.description: The TSA security directive Cybersecurity Coordinator: owns the CISA report, the incident response plan, and IT/OT isolation of dispatching and PTC.

roles.name: Chief of Railroad Police (Rail Security Coordinator)
roles.description: Owns trespass, theft and sabotage response, the 24-hour significant security concern report to TSA, and the FBI liaison.

roles.name: Director of Corporate Communications (PIO)
roles.description: Owns community and media messaging, customer and embargo notices, and statements with local officials.

outsideParties: FRA (regional office, hazmat and signal inspectors)
TSA Surface Operations and the TSOC
the FBI field office and JTTF
county emergency management and the LEPC
the state environmental agency and state police

sceneAnchors.public: a small-town main street beside a railroad grade crossing, crossing gates and red signal lights, a freight train passing, residents on the sidewalk, daylight
sceneAnchors.control: inside a railroad dispatching center: rows of dispatcher desks with track-diagram displays, dispatchers wearing headsets, radio consoles, low lighting
sceneAnchors.exterior: a freight rail yard with long strings of tank cars and boxcars, a locomotive idling, a yard tower, ballast and parallel tracks, overcast sky
